title: Design Application of Neural Radiance Fields in Celadon Art Creation
subtitle: 2023 Undergraduate Thesis

mainContent.content: This project is Chen Yuting's undergraduate thesis (Industrial Design track), dedicated to introducing cutting-edge Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) technology into the traditional field of celadon art creation. Addressing the limitations of existing ceramic auxiliary software in realistically reproducing complex optical properties of glazes (such as refraction, multi-layer textures) and ignoring the "randomness" of the firing process, this project proposes a NeRF-based digital solution that achieves high-fidelity reconstruction and editable prediction from physical glaze samples to digital assets.

Core Technology: NeRF-Tex. Utilizing neural network rendering technology to learn voxel information of glaze surfaces from photo pixels, not only restoring geometric shapes but also precisely capturing light propagation effects within glaze layers. Establishing a closed loop of "glaze composition formulation -> actual firing -> scan data -> model training -> render prediction".

Hardware Innovation: Automated Scanning Platform. Independently developed a small automated scanning device specifically for ceramic glaze samples. Including a top scanning base, ceramic piece positioning mechanism, gimbal motor, and electronic control compartment. By controlling the turntable's uniform rotation, multi-angle image data is automatically collected, lowering the barrier for acquiring high-quality NeRF datasets.

Software System: Celadon Glaze Formulation Assistant Platform. Functional modules include: digital adjustment of glaze formulations, glaze surface database (storing and retrieving firing effects of different formulations), render preview (real-time prediction of glaze surface texture under specific lighting and viewing angles based on NeRF models). Collaborating with Master Wu Yumin, Chief Technician of Longquan City, to establish a high-quality dataset based on traditional Longquan celadon formulations.

Core Design Thinking:
1. Bridging "Digital" and "Material": AIGC typically only generates 2D images and cannot handle complex materials with depth like ceramic glazes. This project attempts to fill this gap, enabling AI to understand "materials" rather than just "images".
2. Embracing "Randomness": Traditional CAD pursues completely deterministic results, but the charm of ceramic art lies in the randomness of "kiln variations". By learning from numerous samples, the model attempts to capture and simulate this random aesthetic.
3. Service Design Perspective: Clearly defining target users as novice art creators, craft practitioners, and researchers, aiming to reduce trial-and-error costs and improve communication efficiency through digital tools.
